data.summary: This 10‑week plan starts with the student’s weakest unit—Thermodynamics and Electrochemistry—then cycles through all remaining units, ensuring each appears at least once. Each week is capped at 5 study hours and includes concrete, single‑sitting tasks. The last week is a mixed review and timed practice session to consolidate knowledge before the exam.
data.final_week_advice: Use the final week for full‑length timed practice exams and targeted review of any remaining weak spots identified during the practice sessions.

tasks: Read textbook sections on entropy and Gibbs free energy; write a 200‑word summary of each concept.
Do 10 practice problems on calculating ΔG and ΔS; check answers with the scoring guide.
Sketch a galvanic cell diagram for a Zn/Cu cell; label all components.
Solve 8 calorimetry problems involving endothermic and exothermic processes; record heat changes.

weeks.focus: Move to Chemical Reactions and Stoichiometry
tasks: Write net ionic equations for 5 common reactions; verify with full equations.
Perform a stoichiometry calculation for a reaction with limiting reagent; document steps.
Draw Lewis structures for 6 molecules; calculate formal charges.
Use VSEPR to predict shapes of 4 molecules; sketch 3D models.
Plot concentration vs. time data for a first‑order reaction; determine rate constant.
Write the rate law for a second‑order reaction; explain each term.
Calculate heat capacity for a given substance using calorimetry data.
Solve 5 ideal gas law problems involving temperature and pressure changes.
Determine the equilibrium constant for a given reaction; explain direction of shift.
Set up and solve a reaction quotient problem; compare with K.
Calculate pH for a weak acid solution; show all steps.
Analyze a buffer system; compute pH after adding a strong base.
Re‑solve the 10 ΔG problems from week 1; aim for 100% accuracy.
Write elementary reaction steps for a complex reaction; identify rate‑determining step.
Take a 60‑minute full‑length practice test; time each section.
Review all incorrect answers; rewrite explanations for each mistake.
